title: Grade 8 INTEGRATED SCIENCE — Transformation of Energy (Screen Drama)
body:
EPISODE PACKAGE
====

EPISODE TITLE: TORCH BEFORE HOMEWORK
SUBJECT / TOPIC: INTEGRATED SCIENCE / Transformation of Energy
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
AGE RATING: 10+ (student-safe)
DURATION: 8 minutes
VISUAL STYLE: naturalistic live-action look with clear prop inserts (or 2D/3D cartoon adaptation of the same blocking)

LEARNING TIE-IN: Keep light long enough by choosing the better energy chain

LOGLINE: A blackout forces a family to trace energy transformations in a torch and a solar lamp to finish homework.

WORLD & CAST
----
• Setting / era: INT. rural-urban home at dusk
• SAMUEL: Grade 8 boy racing sunset. Costume: home clothes.
• GRANDPA JOEL: retired electrician, storyteller. Costume: cardigan.
• NEEMA: sister managing solar lamp. Costume: hoodie.

SCREENPLAY
----

SCENE 1 — EXT./INT. OPENING LOCATION — DAY
----
ACTION: SAMUEL enters the world of the story with a clear goal: Keep light long enough by choosing the better energy chain. Camera follows hands and faces, not a chalkboard.

SAMUEL
If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.

GRANDPA JOEL
Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Wide establishing → medium two-shot. Ambient authentic location SFX. Soft hopeful underscore.

SCENE 2 — SAME / NEARBY — DAY
----
ACTION: Obstacle appears. Stakes rise. Props related to the science idea are handled as real objects, not lecture aids.

SAMUEL
It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.

NEEMA
If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Close-ups on props and worried eyes. Tension riser.

SAMUEL
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

GRANDPA JOEL
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 3 — CONFRONTATION — DAY
----
ACTION: WRONG WAY: Samuel leaves a weak torch on, wasting chemical energy as heat. The problem worsens. Meaning stays in action and argument — characters never read notes aloud.

SAMUEL
See? I did what everyone does.

GRANDPA JOEL
And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Handheld urgency. Cut to the failed result.

SCENE 4 — DISCOVERY — DAY/NIGHT
----
ACTION: A clue appears through action — a label, a measurement, a safer method, a remembered rule spoken as dialogue while doing.

GRANDPA JOEL
Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.

SAMUEL
Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Insert shots of evidence. Music shifts from tension to curiosity.

SAMUEL
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

GRANDPA JOEL
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 5 — SECOND ATTEMPT — DAY
----
ACTION: RIGHT WAY: They map chemical→electrical→light and switch to charged solar wisely. Characters perform the corrected action step by step.

SAMUEL
This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.

NEEMA
I can see the difference already.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Cleaner framed shots; success micro-beats.

SCENE 6 — COMPLICATION — DAY
----
ACTION: A new obstacle or time pressure forces them to apply the idea again, proving it was not luck.

NEEMA
We are not done. Another problem just arrived.

GRANDPA JOEL
Same science. Fresh situation. Go.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Parallel cut or ticking clock motif without graphic peril.

SAMUEL
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

GRANDPA JOEL
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 7 — RESOLUTION — DAY
----
ACTION: Payoff: goal achieved. Characters show the result; still no voice-over lecture.

SAMUEL
It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.

GRANDPA JOEL
Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Warm wider shot; relieved faces; result hero insert.

SCENE 8 — BUTTON — DAY
----
ACTION: Final acted beat tying emotion to the learning without reading notes aloud.

NEEMA
Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.

SAMUEL
And we will check the evidence first.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Slow push-in; music resolves.

SAMUEL
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

GRANDPA JOEL
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

BOOKENDS
----
• COLD OPEN (max 10s): Quick hook image of the failed first attempt — then cut to title TORCH BEFORE HOMEWORK.
• CLOSING REFLECTION CARD (max 10s): On-screen question — What energy chain occurs in a simple torch? Answer must match lesson solutions (Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)).

CAPTIONS
----

GRANDPA JOEL: Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.
SAMUEL: It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.

SAMUEL: This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.

NEEMA: We are not done. Another problem just arrived.
GRANDPA JOEL: Same science. Fresh situation. Go.

GRANDPA JOEL: Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.

SAMUEL: And we will check the evidence first.

ASSET LIST
----
• Characters: SAMUEL, GRANDPA JOEL, NEEMA
• Costumes: as listed above
• Locations: INT. rural-urban home at dusk
• Props: topic-authentic objects for Transformation of Energy
• Key shots: failed attempt insert, evidence insert, successful payoff insert

Study pages available for fidelity: 20
DRAMA NOTE: No voice-over of lesson notes. Meaning travels through action and in-character dialogue.
